notes: The SHORT, on the v2 plate kit. Every `plate` here is a registry key and
every `bind` target is a slot that plate DECLARES — the renderer puts the
text in the slot and does nothing else. Type is set in the face, size,
weight and colour role the kit declares for that slot's role, so the
character budgets are the kit's own `maxChars` rather than something
measured by running a fitter over this file.
THE VERTICAL SET IS TEN FAMILIES, NOT THE WHOLE KIT. The comps table, the
scatter, the waterfall, the grouped bars, the flow plate and the diff
plate are 16:9 by design: they need horizontal room to be readable and
they do not belong in seventy-five seconds. Nothing here reaches for one.
Positions and type sizes are fractions of FRAME HEIGHT, so one template
holds at any delivery resolution. Large type and the caption band never
coexist: a shot carrying type at 6.5% of frame height or more sets
captions false, and the parser refuses the template if it does not.
THE HOST IS IN FOUR SHOTS AND THE CLOSE-UP CARRIES THE TURN. He was in the
cold open, the payoff and the close, all three at full figure in a wide
room — which is the shot you use when the room is the point. The turn is
the line the whole cut rests on and it was being told on bare ground with
nobody in it. `host/close-up` is head and shoulders and it exists for
exactly that beat.

shots.notes: The hook card is the format's own opener — three treatments, and which one a video gets is a property of the script, not of this file.

The price, as a path through the figures the data carries. `plot-area` is a data region: it takes the series and the renderer draws it, which is not the renderer computing anything — it is being handed one.
A headline on paper, in the band drawn for it. Three treatments exist so two headlines in one video are not the same picture twice.
The line the cut rests on, told to camera in close-up. Allowed to be empty — a video with no turn drops this shot rather than holding an empty frame.

One row per shot: the band lights and the frame moves to it. Steps that differ only by which row carries a rectangle are one shot with extra runtime — but a vertical sheet's row is already the width of the frame, so the move is a pan rather than a zoom past the figures. No host: there is no room for a figure in front of a wall-sized sheet, and he returns at the payoff.
Pull back: every row up at once, after the walk down them.
What the sheet meant, in the plate drawn for a line worth pulling out. The numbers comment is written at two hundred characters and there is nowhere on a sheet to put one.
Two things that are both true at once. The plate the format opens on more than any other.
The one figure the video is about, at the size it deserves.
Resigned, not conclusive. The handle sits under it where the date label goes.
